messages:
anya: quick sync — we need to decide how we handle trace id obfuscation for public telemetry exports. privacy asked for no raw ids in exported logs; security wants irreversible masks.

derrek: tl;dr: irreversible hashing (sha256) vs reversible mapping table. both have different cost/ingest/query tradeoffs.

liz: important: cost attribution & deduping rely on stable identifiers. if we irreversibly hash with a per-tenant salt we keep stability but lose ability to map back for debugging.

zach: product note: customers want both privacy and the ability to correlate traces with internal tickets. reversible only available behind enterprise support?

mike: infra perspective: reversible mapping requires an extra lookup store during ingest (or a sidecar that emits both masked and raw). that increases write QPS and storage, and creates an access control burden.

anya: proposal idea: deterministic salted HMAC per-tenant for exported trace_id, and store raw->token mapping in a short-lived encrypted cache accessible to SRE/audit only. fallbacks: if mapping unavailable, fall back to hashed id only.

derrek: tradeoffs: salted HMAC keeps grouping semantics (same raw -> same mask) which preserves split-by and cost attribution. but it still prevents us from recovering original trace_id unless we store raw mapping.

liz: downside: the mapping cache is a sensitive surface — we need strict ACLs, KMS-wrapped keys, and audit logs. Also how long do we keep mapping? 7 days? 30 days? longer helps debugging but increases risk.

mike: ops cost estimates: mapping cache with 7 day TTL at current volume ~ additional 120GB/day of encrypted blobs and ~3k rps at peak for lookups during ingestion. adds ~10% infra spend.

anya: question: do we need reversibility by default or opt-in per org? my vote = opt-in (enterprise) + requestable audit window (manual support flow). default: salted HMAC only.

derrek: sampling implications: if we hash on trace_id only, sampling/reconstruction downstream works. but if we later roll forward to include span-id parts this will change cardinality and effect cost buckets. need a migration plan.

liz: rollout playbook idea:
- step 1: start exporting salted-HMAC-only for all customers for public telemetry sinks (no mapping).
- step 2: add mapping-cache feature behind feature-flag for 10 pilot customers (enterprise).
- step 3: if pilot OK, expose admin opt-in in console with retention knob.

mike: implementation sketch (pseudo header):
```
X-Trace-Id-Raw: 0123abcd...
X-Trace-Id-Export: hmac_sha256(tenant_salt, X-Trace-Id-Raw)[:16]
```
ingest pipeline adds X-Trace-Id-Export to events and drops raw for public sinks unless mapping cache retention is enabled.
```
INSERT INTO ingest_stream (trace_export_id, ...) VALUES (...)
```

zach: customer UX: console needs clear language — "We obfuscate trace ids by default. You can enable reversible trace retention for debugging (enterprise only)." Also show retention period and audit log link.

anya: open questions:
- exact export ID length (first 16 bytes of hmac?) vs full hex (cardinality vs index size)
- retention defaults (7/30/90d) and cost adders
- what queries rely on original format (regex, prefix lookups) that break with hashed tokens

derrek: about length: truncating to 16 bytes is reasonable for index size but increases collision risk — need to calculate collisions at our 10B trace scale. preliminary calc: negligible but run numbers.

liz: telemetry & alerts: update existing SLO/alert runbooks to use trace_export_id where applicable. instrument a reconciliation job that flags missing mappings on opt-in customers.

mike: security checklist: KMS keys per-region, tight IAM roles for mapping read, observability on mapping access, automatic key rotation.

anya: next steps: derrek + mike to run collision and cost estimates. liz to draft mapping access control checklist. I'll draft the rollout RFC for eng-platform + security and link a small PoC that emits both headers for dev only.

ingest-bot: deploy queued: commits/trace-obfuscation-poC -> staging (runbook attached) :rocket:

zach: thanks — please cc me on RFC. important to get security wording and product opt-in flows right. :thumbsup:

anya: packing up — will post RFC link in #eng-platform when ready.
